title: Heisenberg: The Uncertainty Principle - review
transcript: don't let the title of simon steven's new play put you off this is a love story admittedly an unlikely one it's not a stereotypical romantic comedy designed to tug at your heartstrings it's more of a study of two apparently incompatible people a wild 40-something woman and a buttoned-up old man who start by thinking they want one thing but end up finding another the characters and their relationship are complex and contradictory and there's a strong sense that much lies between the lines as the man says of great music it exists in the spaces between the notes this calls for masterful nuanced acting and that's what we get from anne marie duff and kenneth cranham listening to them is like hearing a violin and cello recital the play shows reflecting heisenberg's quantum mechanics that we can only ever think we know people and we can't predict how they behave and there's a lot to savor in noticing how your first impression of the characters her unbearably loud him boringly quiet changes as you get to know them and see them react to each other and there is pathos in the losses that have shaped their lives and a lot of humor particularly about getting old i give it five stars you
